# Spaced Repetition with Leitner Boxes

The cheapest possible spaced-repetition scheduler: every card sits in one of five numbered boxes,
each box has a fixed review interval, a correct answer promotes the card one box, and a wrong
answer sends it **straight back to box 1**. No difficulty rating, no ease factor, no per-card
history — the box number *is* the memory.

## The implementation in [[physics-exam-prep]]

`js/app.js` is 82 flashcards and about ten lines of scheduler:

```
const SR_INTERVALS=[0, 0, 8*60, 24*3600, 3*24*3600, 7*24*3600]; // sec, index by box 1..5
...
box = good ? Math.min(5,box+1) : 1;
const due = Date.now() + SR_INTERVALS[box]*1000;
```

| Box | Next review | Meaning |
|:--:|---|---|
| 1 | immediately | missed, or never seen |
| 2 | 8 minutes | same-session re-check |
| 3 | 1 day | overnight consolidation |
| 4 | 3 days | — |
| 5 | 7 days | "mastered"; the dashboard counts box-5 cards as the mastery number |

Per-card state is `{box, due}` in `localStorage` under `physprep.v1`. The deck is ordered due-first,
then by box, so the weakest material is always on top. The dashboard renders the box distribution
as five pills plus a due count, which turns the scheduler into the progress metric — there is no
separate notion of "cards learned".

## Why this shape fits the constraint

Leitner is the algorithm you choose when the deliverable must run with no network, no server and no
account — [[offline-first-static-deliverable]]. SM-2 and its descendants need a per-card ease factor
and a review log to converge; Leitner needs one integer. It survives a cleared `localStorage` by
resetting to box 1 for everything, which is the correct failure mode for a study tool and needs no
recovery code.

The interval ladder here is also tuned to the actual use: 8 minutes for box 2 is not a memory
interval, it is a *same-sitting* re-check. Combined with the app's own honest estimate of ≈35–45
hours of study over 2–3 weeks, the 7-day top interval means a card can reach "mastered" roughly
twice inside the study window — the ladder is sized to the exam, not to long-term retention.

## Placement

One of the recurring components of [[course-as-runnable-study-tool]], alongside `localStorage`
progress, hash routing and a generated question bank. Only the Physics instance implements Leitner
boxes; the sibling apps track progress without a repetition schedule.

`confidence: high` — the intervals, promotion rule and dashboard behaviour were read directly from
`js/app.js`, and the 82-card count agrees across both READMEs.
